operationName: Ebola PHEIC Response — 2026 Bundibugyo Outbreak, DRC & Uganda
heroHeadline: 291 Confirmed Cases — MSF Opens Goma ETC as Five Survivors Discharged and International Protocols Triggered
heroSubtitle: By 1 June 2026, the 2026 DRC-Uganda Bundibugyo virus (BDBV) outbreak reached 291 total lab-confirmed cases (282 DRC: 264 Ituri, 15 Nord-Kivu, 3 Sud-Kivu; plus 9 Uganda), with 43 confirmed deaths and 220 additional suspected cases under investigation in DRC. Médecins Sans Frontières announced a major scale-up: an 80-bed ETC opened in Goma on June 1 with first patients admitted, a 65-bed ETC under construction in Ituri, and two additional ETCs being established in Bukavu and Lwiro, South Kivu. Five Ebola survivors were discharged as of June 1 — four nurses formally released from hospital plus a lab worker cleared on May 29 — providing evidence that intensive supportive care can achieve recovery even without licensed BDBV-specific therapeutics. Internationally, suspected cases in Italy (Sardinia) and Brazil (São Paulo and Rio de Janeiro) triggered emergency protocols, with all three testing negative for Bundibugyo virus. The 4-week Uganda-DRC border closure entered its fifth day as WHO reiterated that enhanced screening remains epidemiologically superior to blanket closures.
footerNote: Data sourced from WHO Disease Outbreak News (DON602–DON605), DRC Ministry of Health (MSANTE), Uganda Ministry of Health, CDC Ebola Situation Summary, ECDC, MSF, UN News, NPR, CNN, ABC News, and ReliefWeb. Case counts are rapidly evolving.
